table.ruleA: 6 segments, capacities 10,8,12,6,9,7; upper 7,6,9,5,7,5; lower 3,2,4,2,3,2; start 3,6,6,2,2,1; limit 38; all QUIET; tally 0; divisions round down
table.ruleB: 6 crucibles, same capacities, marks, starts and limit 38; all BASE; slag 0; the general rule rounds quarters and halves down (Step 5 overrides it for the tap)

table.ruleA: Add the cycle row to each segment; capacity not enforced
table.ruleB: Add the cycle row to each crucible; capacity not enforced

table.ruleA: In order 1 to 6, one at a time; excess over holding volume (strictly more) moves to n+1 and arrives before n+1 is handled; segment set to its capacity; excess from 6 goes to the loss tally
table.ruleB: In order 1 to 6, one at a time; excess over working volume (strictly more) moves to the next crucible and arrives before that crucible is handled; crucible set to its capacity; excess from 6 goes to slag

table.ruleA: Read after step 2; QUIET at or above the upper mark becomes SINK-ACTIVE; SINK-ACTIVE at or below the lower mark becomes QUIET; at most one change; logged
table.ruleB: Read after Step 2; BASE at or above the upper mark becomes SUPERHEATED; SUPERHEATED at or below the lower mark becomes BASE; at most one change; logged

table.ruleA: Amounts from sap at the start of the step using the state after step 3: QUIET floor(1/4), SINK-ACTIVE floor(1/2); all computed first, then applied together; QUIET amount to loss; SINK-ACTIVE amount to n-1; segment 1 SINK-ACTIVE amount to loss
table.ruleB: Same: BASE floor(1/4) to slag, SUPERHEATED floor(1/2) to the previous crucible (crucible 1 to slag); computed simultaneously, applied at once

table.ruleA: If the total is strictly greater than 38, every segment (all six) becomes floor(sap/2); the removed amount ceil(sap/2) goes to loss; the cycle is logged
table.ruleB: If the total is strictly greater than 38, every crucible (all six) becomes ceil(melt/2) ('half of its melt, rounded up'); the removed amount floor(melt/2) goes to slag; the cycle is logged
table.difference: A keeps half rounded down and B keeps half rounded up, so any odd amount at a halving ends 1 unit higher in B and the loss/slag tally is 1 lower per odd position. This then spreads into later states, triggers and tallies.

table.ruleA: (a) end sap 1-6, (b) end states, (c) state changes in order, (d) leaf-drop cycles, (e) loss tally, (f) balance check
table.ruleB: (a) end melt 1-6, (b) end states, (c) state changes, (d) emergency tap cycles, (e) slag total, (f) balance check

The small rows that follow give odd amounts at the halvings, so the halving's rounding direction shows up. The heavy row in cycle 4 forces a second halving. The probe also exercises the in-order cascade, the 6-to-loss exit and state changes in both directions at position 6.
